summary: A row of controls that act on one thing, reached as one tab stop: arrow keys between the controls, Tab out in one press, and back to the control used last.
useWhen: a set of actions on one selection or one record — the batch bar over a table, a run's Resume/Pause/Stop, an editor's formatting
the row has enough controls that tabbing through each one costs a keyboard user more than it gives

useInstead.when: the row holds a search field or filters
useInstead.why: Tab leaves a toolbar in one press and ← → belong to the caret, so a text field inside strands every filter after it — WAI-ARIA's own caution

useInstead.when: two or three actions in a dialog, drawer or form footer
useInstead.why: a few actions are expected to be a tab stop each; ButtonGroup gives them the gap, the order and a narrow-screen behaviour without the arrow-key model

useInstead.when: two or three actions at the top of a page
useInstead.why: its `actions` slot is a row of ordinary tab stops, which for a few buttons is what a keyboard user expects

useInstead.when: the controls are one choice among options
useInstead.why: that is a radio group with a selected value; a toolbar holds independent actions

composition.note: Buttons in the order they are read, a vertical Divider between groups, and a MenuTrigger with an icon-only Button last for the overflow. Name it with `aria-label` for what it acts on — "Bulk actions", not "Toolbar".
composition.example: <Toolbar aria-label="Bulk actions"><Button size="sm" variant="secondary">Pause</Button><Divider orientation="vertical" /><Button size="sm" variant="destructive">Delete 3</Button></Toolbar>

horizontal.use: the default — ← → move between controls; wraps rather than overflowing

vertical.use: a side rail of tools — ↑ ↓ move between controls

children.note: a nested Toolbar becomes a named `group`, and the outer toolbar keeps the arrow keys

guarantees: React Aria's `useToolbar`: arrow keys move between controls, skipping disabled ones and separators, and are mirrored in right-to-left
Tab leaves the whole toolbar in one press, and Shift+Tab or Tab back in returns to the control used last
a text field, native select, combobox, slider or radio inside keeps its own arrow keys — the caret moves and the value changes instead of focus jumping
↓ still reaches a MenuTrigger in a horizontal toolbar, so an overflow menu opens as it does anywhere else
requires: `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` naming what the toolbar acts on

antiPatterns.dont: a table's search field and filters inside a Toolbar
antiPatterns.why: Tab from the search field leaves the toolbar, so the filters after it can only be reached by Shift+Tab and arrows
a single stop gains nothing from arrow keys, and screen readers announce a toolbar the user has to learn
"toolbar" alone does not say what the buttons act on, and pages with two cannot be told apart
